description.narrative:
Myanmar's education is experiencing substantial challenges largely due to political conflicts and social dynamics exacerbated by the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020 followed by the military takeover in 2022. The compounded crises have worsened systematic challenges and increased educational inequalities at all levels of education and across the country. Specifically, the Myanmar's education is marked by long lasting disruption to formal education that results in a large share of children relying on various forms of non-formal education, either to compensate a lack of formal education or complement it. Despite formal and no-formal possible pathways, disparities in education access reportedly persisted among different population groups. 7.8 millions of children were estimated as out of school children in 2022. Across displaced population groups throughout the country, 16-38% of school aged (6-17 years old) children and youth did not access any type of education. Notably, only 31% of Non-Displaced Stateless People girls had limited access to any type of secondary education whereas 62% of boys accessed education.
The purpose of the SCG project is to strengthen the capacity and resilience of Myanmar's education sector through improving education planning, financing and coordination to create a more inclusive and equitable system. The primary support of the SCG are development and humanitarian nexus partners working within the Myanmar's education sector, including local NGOs, CSOs and INGs and UN agencies.
The SCG project aligns with the Joint Response Framework 2022-2025 and builds upon the ESPDG, integrating insights from the recent studies focusing on Myanmar's education sector to design three key components: advancing a new JRF for 2025-2028, enhancing coordination and response mobilization, and fostering capacity development through a robust data and information system. Specifically:
1. Development and implementation Joint Response Framework (JRF) 2025-2028: In the absence of national education sector plan, JRF will serve as strategic guidance to the partners to ensure children and youth's access to quality with a focus on girls, and children and youth with disability, marginalized and vulnerable groups, including IDP and equitable education during amidst ongoing crises. 2. Strengthen coordination and resource mobilization: In order to enhance Myanmar's education sector through improved coordination, stakeholders' collaboration, and resource mobilization, restructuring key educational sector groups and implementing effective governance mechanisms. This includes efforts for mobilizing resources through strategic partnerships and advocacy to support sustainable educational initiatives. 3. Develop capacity on data and information through developing and implementing data & information platform with a focus on supporting NGOs and CSOs in planning, budgeting, implementing, monitoring and reporting.
